answer: Use a postal-verified address bond. A new agent registers one mailing address and the network posts a sealed cipher code to it, a relic from a slower internet. The agent enters the code within 14 days, the address locks to that one profile, and a second profile at the same address is refused. Re-verification repeats every 180 days. Forging 10,000 identities needs 10,000 rented mailboxes at $15 a month, $150,000 monthly, plus $20,000 postage and a two-week wait per batch. It is like faking a town by renting every post box on its main street, a fable that ends when someone checks the mail.
